selection.name: C01 — Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Canonical WSL image)
selection.role: Provisional co-finalist for the base distribution. Verified vendor image, checksum, documented WSL installation, and five-year standard LTS support.

basis.shows: API-verified catalog blob 47315eb9a5ff3dbf954e609a46d2aa61f429e87d lists the exact Canonical amd64 image at releases.ubuntu.com/26.04.1/ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.wsl, SHA-256 48d56724b5c8e60f24893e83e73bbb58c60b3ca22fba3da977075420acd54104, and a separate arm64 image.
Documents automatic SHA-256 verification for online installation and manual Get-FileHash verification for downloaded images. Verify the downloaded image before running the installation command.
Documents five years of standard support for numbered Ubuntu LTS releases and identifies 26.04 LTS as the current Ubuntu WSL family.
Ubuntu's WSL repository is unarchived; its latest default-branch commit was 2026-08-28, within 90 days. This establishes launcher-source currency, rather than an image-specific test result.
An upstream E2E suite covers instance registration, setup, and restart. Its existence does not establish that this exact image passed on the target host.
A successful August 28 metadata/assets check was observed. It is release infrastructure evidence, not a systemd-user, GPU, or toolchain evaluation.
An upstream Store-version issue was closed and updated on 2026-08-29, providing recent issue activity.
Documents systemd support for sufficiently recent WSL versions. Successful systemd user services on this exact image and host remain unmeasured.

selection.name: C02 — Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (Canonical WSL image)
selection.role: Provisional co-finalist. It has the same verified vendor-image, checksum, installation, and standard LTS support evidence; retrieved measurements do not separate it from the newer LTS image.

basis.shows: The verified catalog lists the exact Canonical amd64 image at releases.ubuntu.com/24.04.5/ubuntu-24.04.5-wsl-amd64.wsl, SHA-256 bb415d824822c4b878125729af451a5d18fb13d1cf5cbed9a7393ad64ac6039e, and a separate arm64 image.
The documented five-year standard-support policy applies to numbered LTS releases, including this release family.
Lists Ubuntu-24.04 and documents installation of downloaded .wsl images through --from-file.
Documents checksum verification; compare the downloaded file's SHA-256 with the catalog digest before installation.
Shares Ubuntu's maintained WSL implementation, whose latest default-branch commit was within 90 days.
The upstream launcher E2E workflow uses windows-2025. No retrieved passing result demonstrates this exact point-release image's target-host behavior.

not_selected.name: Debian 13 (WSL distribution)
not_selected.reason: Provisional: the verified vendor catalog provides Debian amd64/arm64 images and checksums, but labels the installer generically; this research did not verify its Debian 13 base, security lifecycle, or complete required toolchain path sufficiently to prefer it over the documented Ubuntu LTS options.

not_selected.name: Arch Linux (WSL distribution)
not_selected.reason: Its official README documents rolling releases, systemd, and monthly images, and pipeline 179549 passed on October 1; a fixed multi-year security-support commitment was not verified, giving it weaker documented fit for this requirement. Sources: https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/archlinux-wsl/-/blob/27c3224bd240dc056855165d56c263b89bb81725/README.md and https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/archlinux-wsl/-/pipelines/179549.

not_selected.name: Fedora (WSL distribution)
not_selected.reason: Provisional: Fedora 44 vendor images and checksums are verified in the WSL catalog, but its security lifecycle and vendor-source maintenance were not successfully verified; the available evidence does not establish preference over the documented LTS options.

layers.deciding_comparison: Install the exact checksum-pinned Ubuntu 26.04.1 and 24.04.5 images on the same Windows host with WSL 2.7.13 and kernel 6.18, using the same bootstrap. Compare installation and first-boot success/time, updates and restart, a lingering systemd user service, supported provisioning and smoke tests for Python 3.13, Node 24 and current Rust, Claude Code/Codex CLI operation, and nvidia-smi plus the same CUDA workload on the RTX 4090. No unique winner or measured performance superiority is established.
evidence_gaps: The required ctx_fetch_and_index action was rejected with 'MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never'; the requested fetch-and-search workflow could not be completed. Findings therefore rely on accessible upstream API records and source files, and the selection is provisional.
The packet contains no comparison in which every named arm ran. No retrieved benchmark compares these exact images on the target host.
Exact Python 3.13, Node 24 and current Rust provisioning was not verified for either selected image. Canonical's documented apt installation of Node does not establish Node 24.
Node v24.10.0 BUILDING.md says GNU/Linux binaries should work under WSL but treats WSL as unsupported. This caveat applies across the candidates.
Systemd documentation establishes support, rather than successful user-service operation on the specified host. NVIDIA WSL capability does not establish an RTX 4090 result for either exact image.
The documented base-image installation commands run on the Windows host. An upstream-documented native Linux installation command for creating this Windows WSL instance was not verified.
Arm64 WSL catalog entries do not establish native macOS arm64 support. That secondary-host behavior was not verified.
No distro-specific Claude Code/Codex integration or client smoke-test result was verified.

Debian and Fedora vendor-source archive status, latest default-branch commit, release activity and issue activity remain unverified. Recent microsoft/WSL activity establishes catalog/runtime maintenance, not each vendor's maintenance.
Arch's latest main commit was 2026-09-25 and its October 1 pipeline succeeded, but archive status and a latest-release record were not established.
Ubuntu/WSL releases/latest returned a launcher release from 2022; that is not evidence that current Ubuntu vendor images are stale. Exact LTS support end dates were not verified.
Budget used: 6 web-search queries, 6 unsuccessful page-fetch attempts, 20 GitHub API calls, and 10 additional upstream GitLab API attempts.
